title: Complexe de De Rham à puissance divisée [conférence de 1976 à l’IHÉS] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
This page is not Grothendieck's own mathematics. It is the last page (numbered '-4-') of a typed short note by an author at the Institut Central de Mathématique, 14 rue de l'Académie, Bucarest, Roumanie. The bibliography is handwritten and cites Bourbaki AC, EGA IV, Samuel's seminar 1966/67 and Serre's FAC. The handwritten legend in the corner ('— latine, ○ gothique, ○ grec, ronde') is a typesetting key. It tells the printer that underlined letters are italic Latin and circled letters (here the m of m_A) are Fraktur. That suggests a manuscript prepared for a journal such as the Comptes Rendus, which may have been sent to or through Grothendieck. It ended up in cote 136, between his notes on divided-power De Rham complexes.

The mathematics on the page finishes the proof of a lemma and states a corollary.

Setting of the lemma: A is a noetherian local ring with maximal ideal m_A. P^• is a complex of finite flat (hence free) A-modules, bounded above at degree q_0. The hypothesis is that P^•/m_A P^• is exact except in top degree.

The lemma concludes that the top cohomology H is A-flat and that the reduction commutes with taking H.

Steps of the proof:
- **Truncation.** One replaces P^{q_0} by P'^{q_0}, the image submodule. Since P'^{q_0}/m P'^{q_0} → P^{q_0}/m P^{q_0} is injective, the truncated complex ... → P^{q_0-2} → P^{q_0-1} → P'^{q_0} → 0 again satisfies the hypotheses. So one may assume P^q = 0 for q > q_0.
- **Flatness.** The local criterion of flatness (Bourbaki AC Ch. III §5) is then used to show H is A-flat. P^• is a flat resolution of H, so Tor^A_•(A/m_A, H) is the cohomology of P^•⊗A/m_A = P^•/m_A P^•. Vanishing of the higher Tor_1 gives flatness by the local criterion.

Corollary: let f: X → Y be a proper flat morphism of algebraic varieties. Then G_f(Y) = {y ∈ Y : X_y is Gorenstein} is open in Y. Presumably this is proved by applying the lemma to a complex computing a relative dualizing or Ext object. Openness of the Gorenstein locus of fibres for flat finite-type morphisms, combined with properness so that the image of the closed bad locus is closed, gives the statement.
errors: Cohomological indexing (P^q, 'cohomologie') is mixed with homological Tor_•; this is harmless up to reindexing.

Only the end of the proof is visible, so the full hypotheses of the lemma (on pages 1-3, not shown) cannot be checked. The visible argument is the standard truncation plus local flatness criterion and appears correct.

ideas.what: Flatness of top cohomology of a bounded complex of finite free modules via reduction mod m and the local flatness criterion
ideas.modern_name: Local criterion of flatness / cohomology and base change type lemma (cf. EGA III 7, Mumford's Abelian Varieties §5)

ideas.what: Openness of the set of y such that the fibre X_y is Gorenstein, for f proper and flat
ideas.modern_name: Openness of the Gorenstein locus of fibres (relative dualizing sheaf invertible)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Standard; follows from EGA IV §12-type arguments and relative duality (Hartshorne RD; Watanabe-Ishikawa-Tachibana-Otsuka 1969 for related results)
ideas.where_published: Analogous openness statements for CM, S_k, regular fibres in EGA IV 12.1-12.2; Gorenstein not explicitly listed there to my knowledge

missed.claim: This page belongs to a typed paper by a Bucharest author on openness of the Gorenstein fibre locus, apparently a manuscript prepared for publication (it carries printer's markup). It is misfiled within Grothendieck's divided-power De Rham notes in cote 136. It is not Grothendieck's work.

missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Archival cataloguing: attributing this page to Grothendieck would be an error. It may document Grothendieck's role in refereeing or transmitting notes from Romanian algebraists.

deep.surprise_reason: The mathematics is a routine known result (openness of the Gorenstein fibre locus via the local flatness criterion) by a third party. The only point of interest is the archival misplacement.
transcription_corrections: 'l'énoncé que P^? = 0' should read 'P^q = 0 pour q > q_0'.
The circled m in the image indicates Fraktur m_A, which the transcription renders correctly as \mathfrak{m}_A.
The legend '— latine / ○ gothique / ○ grec / ronde' is a typographer's markup key, not mathematical content.
The handwritten date in the bibliography for Bourbaki reads '1961'.
